verdict.rationale: Cursor documents isolated execution environments where agents can test changes. Cloud Agents run in isolated VMs with full dev environments, and they can start dev servers, click through UI flows and verify changes before pushing a PR. Auto-review sandboxes shell commands under file and network limits, and worktrees keep the main checkout untouched. Hooks can gate risky operations such as SQL writes, and permission tokens can deny reads of `.env*` secrets. Missing for 10: an explicit guarantee or documented pattern that separates test runs from production data or credentials (e.g., a sandbox/test-mode data tier; session envVars could still carry production credentials), independent or hands-on corroboration, and the docs' own note that 'Auto-review is not a security boundary.'
